topology: PC1 reaches the prepared HTTP server through two directly connected IPv4 LANs on R1. The learner automates restoration of R1 Gi0/1 while preserving Gi0/0 as a negative control. Addresses, gateways and HTTP are prepared; no routing protocol or static-route shortcut is configured.
implemented: Automation is the seventh ENCOR section with one lab,39 ENCOR entries and accessible singular counts. Existing category order and original CCNA authentication labs are retained. Permalinks preserve the current domain, path and query.

RESTORE uses event none and seven explicitly padded action labels, enters privileged/configuration/interface modes, restores Gi0/1, sets its description and emits a real HA_EM syslog. Actual outage, failed probes, a real admin-down to admin-up change and three fresh client replies prove manual recovery.

RECOVER uses an anchored syslog regular expression and the same IOS action sequence. Actual new Gi0/1 down logs drive automatic recovery. A Gi0/0 down negative control remains down and requires manual restoration before client traffic resumes.

EEM labels preserve their exact strings, replace/remove by exact label and execute in ascending lexical order, including distinct decimal spellings. Applet edits register on leaving configuration mode, including Ctrl-Z and configuration import.

Syslog detectors use bounded regular-expression matching with literal underscores, anchors, groups, alternation, character ranges and simple quantifiers. Each actual matching log is processed once, even with multiple events in one scan or disabled display buffering. Re-registration starts at the current log cursor rather than replaying old logs. Render/import preserves literal regex backslashes.

Per-applet registration and timer ownership preserve unrelated countdown/watchdog deadlines. Countdown fires once and watchdog repeats. Deletion, power-off and runtime replacement cancel owned callbacks; startup restoration registers fresh timers. Archive scheduling retains separate ownership.

Controlled troubleshooting observes a lexical-label ordering failure, an invalid interface action and a missed syslog pattern. Each repair requires actual later recovery and new delivered client traffic. Correcting a missed pattern alone cannot retroactively revive the old event.

Temporary LAB-WATCH and LAB-ONCE applets demonstrate at least two spaced watchdog executions and one countdown execution across two periods. Learners record these observations while the one-shot applet remains registered, then remove both timers before final save.

Bounded execution evidence retains trigger provenance, applet definition, exact action labels, status, real log identifiers and actual interface field mutations. Executions cap at128 records, detector observations at512, applets at64, actions at100 and recursion/causal chains at8. Self/mutually matching action syslogs cannot create unbounded loops.

Question-mark help and Tab expose implemented none/syslog/countdown/watchdog detector and CLI/syslog action paths. Verification uses native policy/history tables, real interfaces, real logs and saved configuration.

Practice starts0/14. Completed reference provides four live configuration/save goals with no invented events, traffic or fault achievements. All14 earned observations survive YAML export/import while operational histories and detector sessions rebuild. Final save requires exactly the two recovery applets, working links/addresses/gateways/HTTP and R1 startup equality.
scope: IOS EEM applet exercise covering event none, bounded syslog patterns, countdown/watchdog timers, CLI actions and syslog actions. The simulator continues to stop applets on rejected CLI actions; production EEM error-handling and Tcl runtime behavior are outside this lab.
Tcl policies, variables, conditionals, cron, AAA integration, IP SLA/track/hardware-specific EEM detectors and NX-OS event-manager policy syntax are not configured or claimed by this lab.
Primary Cisco IOS and IOS XE documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed; existing IOS/NX-OS CML regression contracts remain in the full native suite.
No UI theme/layout, terminal styling, node artwork, dependency or backend/server changes.
